subject: Streaming probe synthesis + demo schedule (first-token targets & chunk cadence)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Mendez <ella@fastlogix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, May 27, 2026 at 6:02 PM PDT
Subject: Post-call: streaming probe synthesis + action items

Hi Ella / FastLogix team — thanks again for the call today. Quick synthesis and proposed next steps so we have alignment before a technical demo:

Summary / alignment:
- Primary objective: confirm Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target for live chat (low-latency streaming) and validate chunk cadence for SSE pipeline.
- FastLogix target: sub-200ms median for initial token in steady state; acceptable 95th percentile up to 350ms.
- Expected steady concurrency: ~300–450 QPS across your multi-region frontends (peak 600 QPS for 90s bursts).
- Preferred stream transport: SSE for browser clients; WebSocket fallback for mobile SDKs.

Open technical questions we flagged on the call (for our demo readiness):
1) Request/response size distribution: typical prompt lengths and average token counts (you mentioned ~60 tokens answer average).
2) Acceptable initial chunk size: you preferred smaller first chunk (8–12 tokens) and then 32-token cadence — want us to confirm viability at scale.
3) Cold-start tolerance: how many concurrent cold sessions can you tolerate during morning ramp? You said ~50 concurrent cold sessions is realistic.

Attachments: I attached the probe results matrix we ran against a representative prompt set and a draft demo agenda (streaming_probe_results.xlsx; demo_agenda.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- Ben / Karthik to run a focused probe replicating your concurrency profile (300–450 QPS) and measure median/95th TTFT with our SSE path and with a WebSocket fallback. Target completion: EOD Tue, Jun 1.
- Schedule a 30-minute technical demo to drive through real traces and live load (Calendly link below). Proposed window: next Wed/Thu morning PT.
- FastLogix to share sample prompts and any priming heuristics you use (role-play system prompt, persona length).

If that looks right I’ll schedule the demo and we’ll follow with a brief mutual action plan for an initial pilot.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

---
Attachments: streaming_probe_results.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB), demo_agenda.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Ella Mendez <ella@fastlogix.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: FastLogix Solutions <ops@fastlogix.com>
Date: Fri, May 28, 2026 at 8:06 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming probe synthesis + action items

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear write-up. Confirming a few items and answering the open questions from our side: 

- Prompt/token profile: conversational prompts, median prompt ~35 input tokens, output median ~60 tokens. We do occasional long responses (~400 tokens) for receipts/summary flows but those are <5% of traffic.
- First chunk preference: yes, we tend to prefer a small initial chunk (8–10 tokens) so UI can render quickly, then 24–32 token chunks thereafter.
- Cold-start tolerance: 50 concurrent cold sessions is correct during our peak. We can accept a slightly higher tail during a morning ramp but want predictable fallback behavior.
- Transport: SSE for web is primary. Mobile apps will use WebSocket when available. Important: keep chunking consistent across both transports.

We’re happy for Redwood to run the probe. For demo scheduling, Wed Jun 3 10:00 AM PT works for our engineering lead (I’ll add calendar invite after you confirm).

Also attaching a small sample prompt set and a short doc with priming heuristics (I uploaded to ops@fastlogix.com).

Best,
Ella
Head of Product, FastLogix
ella@fastlogix.com

Monica — quick internal note before we kick the probe off:

Thanks for the summary. A couple of implementation notes for the probe design so results map to their production profile:
- Probe scenario: mix of short (~60 token total) and occasional long (~400 token) responses at 95:5 ratio. That matches their traffic.
- Priming: apply their 2-step system prompt (they sent doc to ops@fastlogix.com) during generation to reflect real priming cost for KV cache sizing.
- Chunking experiment matrix: first_chunk = [6,10,12] tokens; followup_chunk = [20,28,32] tokens. Measure median TTFT, 95th TTFT, and token-per-second throughput.
- Transport parity: run probes over both SSE and WebSocket; ensure identical payload framing (we’ll reuse our streaming shim).

I’ll stand up the load scenario today and aim to post preliminary numbers by EOD Tue Jun 1. Karthik — can you validate the KV cache memory settings for the 400-token tails? If not, I’ll default to our medium cache config.

— Ben

- 0–5m: goals & quick design recap (TTFT target, concurrency profile)
- 5–18m: live probe traces (SSE + WebSocket side-by-side) showing first-chunk latency and tail behavior
- 18–25m: chunk cadence trade-offs (spline of token throughput vs observed TTFT)
- 25–30m: next steps & pilot kickoff criteria

Action items (who/when):
- Ben: run probe matrix and upload results to shared drive (due EOD Tue Jun 1).

I’ll send a brief mutually agreed acceptance checklist after demo (minimum: median TTFT < 200ms; 95th < 350ms; consistent chunking across transports; successful fallback behavior under cold-start ramp).

See you at the demo — Monica
